key_insight: Riemannian Anderson mixing accelerates natural-gradient optimization of neural probability measures by using past residuals to approximate second-order information without forming Hessians.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce optimization effort in sampling, inverse problems, and generative modeling built on neural Wasserstein geometry.
method: Represent probability measures as neural-network pushforwards of a reference distribution.
Equip network parameters with a pullback Wasserstein metric and interpret natural-gradient descent as a manifold fixed-point iteration.
Accelerate updates with Riemannian Anderson mixing using historical residuals.
evidence_signal: Across multimodal sampling, PDE inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling, the abstract reports fewer natural-gradient iterations and competitive gradient-evaluation counts and wall-clock time versus SGD and Adam.
watch_item: Practical speedups may depend on the cost and numerical stability of computations involving the parameter-dependent Wasserstein metric.
paper_title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
